Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement (CUSMA, 2020) — investment and cross-border services chapter
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP, in force for Canada 30 December 2018)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 ('PCMLTFA'), as amended (incl. S.C. 2022, c. 10, Bill C-47 amendments); PCMLTFA Regulations SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.05, 83.08, 462.31; United Nations Act, S.C. 1991, c. 45 (implementation of UN Security Council sanctions); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Freezing and Forfeiture), S.C. 2011, c. 31; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 233.1 (financial/UBO information reporting). Provincial (British Columbia): Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 ('BCA'), ss. 24(1) (name/dosage? — name requirements), 42 (registered office), 51 (unlimited shareholder liability); BCA beneficial ownership transparency amendments and the BC Beneficial Ownership Transparency Registry (in force 1 May 2025, administered with the BC Corporate Registry) imposing the initial and annual UBO records/filings.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Fully_Public — British Columbia maintains a publicly searchable beneficial ownership register (effective 1 May 2025) disclosing individuals who directly or indirectly own or control 25% or more of a company; limited application to withhold/redact information on personal-safety grounds, otherwise all UBO particulars are public.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence / Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign corporate shareholder (e.g., Delaware C-Corp), issued not older than 30 days
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the parent company's home jurisdiction (e.g., Delaware Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the foreign competent authority (e.g., Delaware Secretary of State) under the Hague Apostille Convention of 1961; the Apostille is recognized directly in Canada (Convention in force in Canada since 11 January 2024); no Canadian consular legalization required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the foreign parent's Certificate of Incorporation and Charter Documents (Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-jurisdiction registry or registered agent of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a licensed foreign notary, followed by Hague Apostille from the foreign competent authority; accepted by the BC Registrar without further legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn UBO Statutory Declaration / Beneficial Ownership Transparency Record initial filing (identifying all individuals at the 25% ownership or control threshold, together with date-of-birth, residential address, and identification details)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BC notary public or commissioning lawyer (for signatures taken in Canada); foreign notary (for foreign-signatory declarations)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Provincial notarization/commissioning; if executed outside Canada, additional Hague Apostille from the executing state is attached for recognition in BC.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof-of-address of all proposed directors and each UBO (corporate card program senior managers included)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of each individual's country of nationality, with notarial certification of the copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true-copy certification; foreign notarizations must carry a Hague Apostille when they originate in a Convention state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney authorizing the Canadian incorporation agent and named law firm to file the BC incorporation application and ancillary registrations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The foreign parent's board of directors (corporate resolution) or authorized officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of board resolution and notarized execution; if signed outside Canada, the notarized instrument requires a Hague Apostille for filing in BC corporate registry records.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign legal opinion on the parent's legal existence, capacity, and beneficial ownership chain (corporate pierce-through evidence from parent to ultimate natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: External counsel in the parent's home jurisdiction (e.g., US counsel for a Delaware C-Corp)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Counsel's original opinion with notarized counsel signature; apostilled when the registry or bank sponsor requires formal legalization of counsel capacity.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening against: (i) FINTRAC PEP categories under PCMLTFA s. 54.1 — domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs, and heads of international organizations — with enhanced measures for foreign PEPs and heads of international organizations, including reasonable measures to establish the source of wealth and source of funds; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List via implementing Canadian regulations under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act (incl. Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, Venezuela, Nicaragua, Myanmar, Sudan, and other global assets-control regimes); (iii) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions, and the Criminal Code s. 83.05 terrorist entity list; (iv) OFAC SDN List and the OFAC 50-percent rule, mandatory for all USD-denominated Mastercard Network and Visa Direct payment rails; (v) FinCEN and EU/UK consolidated lists as supplementary overlays; updated via institutional-grade screening databases (e.g., World-Check, LexisNexis Bridger Insight, Dow Jones) with daily re-screening and adverse-media monitoring; all screening results are documented in the AML/CFT risk file for FINTRAC and the BC regulator.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online operated by the BC Corporate Registry (Province of British Columbia, Ministry of Finance) at corporateonline.gov.bc.ca; name searches run through the NUANS-D database (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) for Canada.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official corporate name must be set in Latin-script characters (English or French format). BC does not register names in non-Latin scripts; a foreign-language brand may appear only as a transliterated Latin-script (English/French) equivalent. The name must not be 'confusingly similar' to existing corporate names, limited partnerships, or registered trademarks, as determined by the NUANS search and the Registrar. For an unlimited liability company, the name must end with 'Unlimited Liability Company', 'ULC', 'Société à responsabilité illimitée', or the French abbreviation where applicable; no other corporate ending is permitted.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK (requires written consent of the Minister of Finance / OSFI under the Bank Act, s. 983)
TRUST / LOAN AND TRUST (federally restricted financial terms requiring ministerial consent)
CREDIT UNION (provincially regulated, incorporation under the Financial Institutions Act required)
INSURANCE / ASSURANCE (financial-services restricted token requiring regulator consent)
ROYAL / PRINCE / PRINCESS / KING / QUEEN / EMPEROR (Crown-implication terms requiring prior ministerial approval)
UNIVERSITY / COLLEGE / INSTITUTE (requires consent of the relevant educational authority)
MUNICIPALITY / MUNICIPAL / POLICE (government affiliation implications; prohibited without government consent)
LAWYER / BARRISTER / SOLICITOR / NOTARY / LEGAL (regulated-profession tokens prohibited without Law Society consent)
CANADA / CANADIAN (national-symbol token; requires approval of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
BRITISH COLUMBIA / VANCOUVER (geographic identifier; requires provincial consent or a legitimate connection to the stated place of business)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC name reservation is valid for 56 days and may be extended once for an additional 56 days before incorporation. If the Registrar rejects the proposed name (e.g., confusion, restricted token without consent, misdescriptive), the applicant may: (i) request a reconsideration ('Request for Reconsideration of Name Decision') through BC Corporate Online or by written submission to the Registrar of Companies within the reservation period, attaching a legal memorandum on non-confusion, consent letters from existing name holders, or the required ministerial approvals; (ii) if reconsideration is refused, file an administrative appeal as a petition for judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, within 60 days of the reconsideration decision, seeking an order setting aside the Registrar's decision; (iii) concurrently reserve a new NUANS-clean name variant at a cost of CAD 30 to avoid delay where commercial timelines are critical.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: BC BCA s. 42 requires a registered office at an address in British Columbia at which the registrar may serve documents; a P.O. Box is disallowed. A virtual-office address supplied by a BC service provider with a physical street address and live reception/records capacity is permissible at incorporation stage. For the B2B virtual-card-issuing business, pure-virtual status will not withstand FINTRAC MSB/PSA registration (Retail Payment Activities Act, S.C. 2021, c. 23, in force 16 November 2024) or Mastercard/Visa program sponsor due diligence; a substantive Canadian place of business, transaction-monitoring capability, and operational substance must be established before licensure and network approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — quantified at approximately 80% probability of a risk-based compliance examination or unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months of obtaining FINTRAC registration and network sponsor approval, reflecting FINTRAC's examination prioritization of high-risk payment-sector entities and the statutory inspection powers under PCMLTFA ss. 65.1–65.2; BC corporate-registry site verifications are also conducted on a risk basis for registered-office addresses.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (British Columbia), particularly s. 3 (unlimited liability company), s. 12 (incorporation application), s. 13 (certificate of incorporation), s. 14 (effect of incorporation), s. 22 (correction of information), and Business Corporations Regulation B.C. Reg. 65/2006. The Canada Business Corporations Act is not applicable as this is a provincial ULC.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Corporate Registry (Registry Services), Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia, Victoria, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 3) filed together with Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles (Form 2) submitted via BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the BC Business Corporations Act; the ULC may be incorporated with nominal share capital. However, as a regulatory and commercial practice, BCFSA and sponsoring card-issuing banks expect the entity to maintain liquid capital or a program collateral bond of approximately CAD 100,000 or equivalent to cover payment obligation and settlement risk. No escrow account is prescribed at the incorporation stage.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Corporation issues and allots 100 Class A Common Shares to the founding shareholder at CAD 1.00 per share, fully paid and non-assessable; RESOLVED: That the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [Registered Address], British Columbia; RESOLVED: That [Founder Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, and [Secretary Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, with the President acting as chief compliance officer for money-services licensing; RESOLVED: That the President, or any one director, is authorized to execute banking agreements, regulatory filings, and card-network applications, and to complete the incorporation filings with the British Columbia Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Online, Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search through the BC Corporate Online portal and file a Name Reservation Request. The system issues a NUANS report and, upon approval, a Name Reservation Number valid for 56 days. The proposed name must contain a distinct and distinctive element and may include the legal element ULC or Unlimited Liability Company.
required_dossiers: Proposed name details including ULC legal element
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusingly similar, select one of the alternate names from the NUANS report and re-file; a written reconsideration may be submitted to the Registrar of Companies for an administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and corporate service provider acting for the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Incorporation Application (Form 3), Notice of Articles (Form 1), Articles (Form 2) reflecting an unlimited liability company, director consents, registered office address, and first director appointments. Each incorporator must execute the incorporation agreement. Notarization is not mandatory for domestic incorporators.
required_dossiers: Form 4 Consent to Act as Director
Registered office consent from the property owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries incomplete fields, revise the affected form and resubmit via Corporate Online; any already paid fees are credited toward the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies via BC Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed statutory documents to the BC Corporate Online portal, pay the CAD 300 incorporation fee (approximately USD 220) and CAD 30 name reservation fee by credit card, and ensure all schedules and consents are attached before electronic submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Notice of Query is issued, respond within 14 days by correcting the deficiency on the registry portal; unresolved queries may be cured by filing corrected information under s. 22 of the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon statutory review approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation containing the BC company number. Obtain certified copies and record the certificate in the corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, apply for a correction of the certificate under s. 22 of the Business Corporations Act with supporting affidavit evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Organizational Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, which may be held by written consent in lieu of a meeting, and adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. Issue the subscribed share certificates, appoint officers, approve the fiscal year end, and authenticate the corporate seal.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or written consent resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Inadvertently invalid resolutions may be ratified by a subsequent board resolution; where officer details change, file the updated register and any required notices with the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Canada Revenue Agency and Provincial Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; BC Corporate Registry; BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the CRA Business Number online through Business Registration Online; register for GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll accounts. Register the provincial corporate account and confirm the annual report cycle. Register for BC PST if taxable services are provided.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA registration queries are cured by filing a corrected CRA RC1A form; registration effective dates can be adjusted upon written explanation accepted by the CRA Business Number unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking, Card Network, and Processor Infrastructure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sponsor bank authorized on Mastercard and Visa networks; PCI-DSS compliant card processor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a commercial deposit account with a Canadian financial institution; execute a BIN sponsorship agreement and an issuing-processor agreement for the virtual corporate card program; complete PCI-DSS SAQ-D assessment; implement transaction screening and program monitoring controls.
required_dossiers: Beneficial ownership register under BC BCA transparency rules
Statement of program capitalization and settlement collateral
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the sponsor bank declines the application, apply to an alternate BIN sponsor; remedy KYC deficiencies with supplementary due diligence documentation or increase the collateral/or collateral trust arrangement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Services Authorization and AML/ATF Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register as a Money Services Business with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; apply for the MSB licence under the BC Money Services Business Act; submit the AML/ATF program, enterprise risk assessment, compliance officer appointment, and business continuity plan; confirm compliance with the Retail Payment Activities Act if applicable.
required_dossiers: Business continuity and data security plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: B.C. deficiencies identified by BCFSA are cured through an approved written corrective action plan; FINTRAC late-registration matters may be resolved by filing with voluntary disclosure and documentation of good-faith compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA) and Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Money Services Business Licence under the Money Services Business Act (British Columbia) and MSB Registration under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (Canada); Mastercard/Visa virtual card BIN sponsorship obtained through a regulated issuer bank

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Division, British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, with reference to Environment and Climate Change Canada
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full environmental assessment — the undertaking is an office-based financial technology activity with no physical industrial footprint and does not meet any threshold in the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2018, c. 51 or the Reviewable Projects Regulation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or industrial effluent discharges; compliance with municipal sewer and solid waste bylaws; zero direct VOC emissions from manufacturing processes; e-waste disposal in accordance with the BC Recycling Regulation (B.C. Reg. 315/2007); office energy use subject to provincial energy-efficiency reporting, with no applicable greenhouse gas emissions threshold for this class of activity

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the BC Fire Code for the leased office occupancy; municipal building occupancy permit confirming structural load and life-safety compliance; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance for the financial-services workplace; annual electrical safety inspection and emergency response plan approval for the premises

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portal: My Business Account (business registration via Business Registration Online at canada.ca) and GST/HST NETFILE; CRA corporate Internet filing for T2 returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the BC ULC under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) via Corporate Online (BC Registry); receive BC incorporation number. 2) Register the corporation with CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1 to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN). 3) Activate program accounts: RP (T2 corporate income tax), RT/RM (GST/HST), RC (payroll), and RP with 'revenue account' if withholding required. 4) A foreign (non-resident) corporation carrying on business in Canada obtains a BN directly from CRA using Form RC1, together with Form T2 (T2 Corporation Income Tax Return) obligations and, where applicable, a Part XIII/NR4 withholding program account (RN). For a BC ULC, standard domestic incorporation registration applies because the entity is incorporated in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A BC ULC is a corporation under the Income Tax Act (Canada), deemed resident in Canada pursuant to ITA s.250(4) (incorporated in Canada after April 26, 1965); it is a 'taxable Canadian corporation' filing a T2 return and subject to federal Part I tax (15% general corporate rate) plus BC provincial corporate income tax (12% general rate; combined ~27%). It is NOT a CCPC if controlled by a non-resident US parent, so the small business deduction is unavailable. For US federal tax purposes the ULC is Pass_Through_Eligible (via check-the-box), creating a hybrid entity; Territorial_Scope: Canada taxes the ULC on worldwide income (treaty relief on foreign income via Part I and foreign tax credits); Tax_Exempt_Zone: none applicable — a virtual card issuer licensed as a money-services business/fintech remains fully taxable in BC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: US federal check-the-box election under Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3 (Form 8832) permitting a BC ULC to be treated as a disregarded entity (pass-through) for US tax purposes while remaining a Canadian corporation for Canadian tax purposes; Canadian GST/HST group registration election under Excise Tax Act s.150 (closely related corporations treated as a single person); election under ETA s.225.2? No — I must be careful. Let me use: 'GST/HST closely related corporation election under ETA s.150; optional section 216(1) election for non-resident property rental income (not applicable to card issuing); hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss.18.3-18.6) limit deduction/no-inclusion outcomes and imported mismatches for hybrid-financed payments.'

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential banking regulation exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), policy oversight by the Department of Finance Canada, and cross-border transaction monitoring by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada abolished its Foreign Exchange Control Board in 1951; no dedicated foreign-exchange control authority now exists. Legal tender, note issuance, and monetary policy are governed by the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility with IMF Article VIII obligations; no approval, quota, or licence is required for inbound equity injections, profit remittance, dividend distributions, or shareholder-loan repayments to non-residents. For the British Columbia ULC (CA_ULC), the only relevant hurdles are (i) Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on actual or deemed distributions (statutory 25 percent, treaty-reduced, e.g., 5 percent for qualifying 10-percent corporate shareholders and 15 percent otherwise under the Canada-US treaty; similar reductions exist under the Canada-UK, Canada-Germany, and other Canada tax treaties), including section 84(2)/(3) deemed-dividend rules for certain ULC distributions to non-residents, and (ii) FINTRAC and Statistics Canada reporting thresholds. No foreign-exchange quota or central-bank approval applies to repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, mandatory conversion ratio, or foreign-exchange repatriation timeline exists in Canada. Exporters and fintech treasury companies may hold foreign currency offshore or in Canadian bank accounts without conversion. Compliance duties are limited to (i) FINTRAC Large Value International Wire Transfer reporting of every international electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more (five-business-day deadline), and (ii) the cross-border currency and monetary instruments report (CBCMIR) for physical movement of currency, cheques, or bearer instruments of CAD 10,000 or more into or out of Canada.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Hybrid Capital Escrow / Operational Account (multi-currency CAD and USD)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (under Section 271 of the Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, British Columbia (corporate registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation or first registration each calendar year (e.g., incorporation April 10 => filing due by June 10)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately USD 74 (CAD 100); continued failure exceeding two consecutive years may trigger administrative strike-off and loss of corporate status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under British Columbia's Business Corporations Act, private companies can waive a statutory audit by unanimous shareholder resolution. However, a virtual card issuing entity operating as a money services business is subject to Canadian regulatory licensing (e.g., FINTRAC MSB registration, Retail Payment Activities Act supervision) which typically requires an annual independent audit as a licensing condition. Accordingly, a certified audit is effectively mandatory for the regulated issuer.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Canada, or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for qualifying private companies; regulated financial institutions and entities with cross-border payment networks are normally expected to apply IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For British Columbia companies, the Business Corporations Act (Part 2.1) requires the company to maintain an internal Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC Register). The register must be reviewed at least annually and updated within 30 days of any share transfer or change in significant control. No external annual filing of the ISC Register is required unless specifically demanded by the registrar or law enforcement; however, the company must be prepared to produce it upon request. Annually, all share movements must be reconciled against the Register of Members and the ISC Register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typical certified audit fee range: $10,000-$25,000 USD for a fintech virtual card issuer
